t: This is St Paul's, a Grade II listed Anglican church on Onslow Square in South Kensington. It was built in 1860, and the architect was James Edmeston. Edmeston was a surveyor as well as an architect, and he was also a prolific writer of church hymns, so he shaped both the building and the words sung inside churches. Later, the composer William Carter became organist here in 1868. And the evangelical clergyman Hanmer William Webb-Peploe served as vicar for 43 years, from 1876 to 1919.
